page.title: Candidates
page.purpose: Judge a candidate set against the legibility gate and select one to proceed. This is where a pretty picture is separated from a usable backdrop.

priorities.statement: The contrast verdict is legible without colour.
priorities.notes: Every verdict shows the measured ratio as a number and a text label alongside any colour encoding. A contrast tool that conveys its own verdicts by hue would fail exactly the users it exists to protect.

priorities.statement: Each candidate reads as a recipe, not an accident.
priorities.notes: Strategy, seed, execution path, and the full resolved plan are attached to every tile and copyable. Two operators looking at the same candidate should be able to reproduce it.

priorities.statement: A specimen is framed against its own declared ground.
priorities.notes: The frame must not inherit the page background, or the same candidate reads differently in light and dark themes and neither reading is trustworthy.

priorities.statement: Selection is explicit even when there is one candidate.
priorities.notes: No auto-selection, so the selection record always names who chose.

states.description: Candidates arrive progressively. Each slot holds its aspect and shows the execution path being used.
Every candidate cleared its threshold. Each shows its measured ratio; selection is available.
Some candidates fail the gate. Failing tiles state measured value, threshold, and the region measured, and offer the minimum scrim that would pass.
No candidate clears the threshold. Offers scrim amendment, a copy-safe region adjustment, or a re-render with a different seed — rather than presenting a dead end.
The render was routed onward because local hardware could not serve it. States which path ran and which model tier served, so a lower-quality result is attributable rather than mysterious.
Execution failed. States the cause reported by image-tools and offers retry, without discarding candidates that already succeeded.
